description: It's been a year since we settled in and my back deck has slowly become my favorite room in the house. My three-bedroom home is nothing showy around 1400 sq.ft., but the walk out basement is full of light, and we love to spend the cool evenings on the back porch. Most mornings I'm out on the upstairs porch off the main living room, coffee growing cold, just watching the stream catch the light. The stream’s constant murmur sold me on this lot before we’d graded the house seat. At 2,400 feet, the hardwoods hold onto a coolness the valley below doesn't get, and I trimmed the rhododendron along the bank so I could see our many visitors. I've learned the creek's morning rhythm. Most mornings I’ll see a doe and her fawn pick their way along the far bank. Wild turkeys work the leaf litter past the tree line. Chipmunks scold me from the rock pile, while the songbirds and Carolina wrens fill the air with song. The occasional pileated woodpecker hammering somewhere up the ridge never really stops. It's the kind of quiet during the day that's full, not empty. At night, it's the other kind of quiet. No streetlights, no traffic, with only two homes above my end of the road means the only thing passing by after dark is the occasional set of headlights pulling into a driveway I recognize. Crickets and katydids take over from the birds, an owl calls from somewhere across the stream, and the stars do what they can't do in town. And yet I'm not alone out here, my neighbors in Pinnacle Mountain View are close enough that someone notices if my lights are off too many nights in a row, close enough to call when a tree comes down across the publicly maintained road. Privacy and community, somehow, in the same acre of woods. On weekends I'm at DuPont or Pisgah admiring the waterfalls, miles of trail, with more biking than I'll ever get through. description: Exchange is a historic waterfront plantation situated in the prestigious Plantersville District of Georgetown County on the banks of the Pee Dee River. The property traces its roots to a 1735 Land Grant from King George II.  Neighboring plantations include Chicora Wood, Breakwater, Rosebank, Hasty Point, Glenmore and Arundel. At its peak in the 1840s this area was producing 50% of the rice exported from America and coastal Georgetown became one of the wealthiest cities in America.,Today, Exchange is known for its hunting, fishing and exceptional beauty. There are open pine woodlands, hardwood forests, clover fields, bass ponds and waterfowl impoundments providing habitat for deer, turkeys, doves and especially all types of ducks. The house and grounds are stunning. The main house and rice barn are on the National Historic Registry.,Exchange has been in the same family for over 80 years. The property is protected by a conservation easement with Wetlands America Trust / Ducks Unlimited.

description: The Norton Farm North offers 30.39+/- acres of productive farmland and woods in the Green Sea area of Horry County, South Carolina. With nearly an even split between cultivated ground and timber, this is the kind of traditional Carolina farm that can serve several purposes for its future owner. Approximately 18+/- acres are currently planted in soybeans, providing immediate agricultural use along with an attractive setting across the open fields. The balance consists of roughly 12+/- acres of wooded land, giving the property a good mix of cover, habitat, and privacy. The transition between the fields and woods creates natural travel corridors and feeding areas for wildlife, with hunting opportunities for whitetail deer, wild turkey, and upland game. The farm has frontage along county-maintained Norton Road, providing convenient year-round access. With no HOA or building restrictions currently in place, a future owner has the flexibility to continue farming the property, establish pasture, build a country home, create a recreational retreat, or simply hold the land as a long-term investment. One of this farms strongest attributes is its location. It sits just 2 miles from Green Sea-Floyds High School and less than 15 minutes from either Loris, SC or Tabor City, NC. Conway, Longs, and Whiteville, NC are all approximately 30 minutes away, while North Myrtle Beach and Lake Waccamaw, NC can be reached in roughly 45 minutes. The Norton Farm North combines productive acreage, wooded habitat, road frontage, and a quiet rural setting while remaining within an easy drive of communities throughout northeastern South Carolina and southeastern North Carolina. For buyers looking for a manageable Horry County farm with agricultural, recreational, and homesite potential, this 30.39+/- acre property deserves a closer look.
